digest.component_or_area: rebar CLI comment and positional-body commands
propositions: rebar comment silently accepts flag-like tokens (--body-file, --body) as the literal comment body instead of rejecting them, destroying the intended content while exiting 0
the stored comment is a short string (6-11 bytes) rather than the actual body, and a content length check appears successful while the record is corrupted
multiple independent sessions have lost work this way, with evidence visible in tickets b690 and session log 55a9
the same vulnerability exists in other positional-body commands (create, edit, session-log, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands) and requires a consistent guard across all of them
a body argument beginning with - must be rejected with non-zero exit and usage guidance, with -- as the documented escape hatch for values that legitimately start with -
the implementation must not silently truncate or coerce: a body that cannot be stored as given must fail loudly and clearly
